question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At the drop of a hat
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"At the drop of a hat"** means to do something instantly or without any hesitation. (तुरंत)

 
 
• **Example: **She would leave her job **at the drop of a hat** if she had a better opportunity.
 
 
 
• **"Immediately"** refers to doing something at once, without any delay. (तुरंत)
 
 
• **Example: **The doctor attended to the patient **immediately** after he arrived.
 
 

Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is** 'Immediately.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Consecutively **(क्रमशः): Following continuously in unbroken or logical sequence.

 
 
• **Example:** She won the championship for three **consecutive** years.
 
 
 
• **Eventually **(अंततः): In the end, especially after a long delay, dispute, or series of problems.
 
 
• **Example: **After many years of hard work, he **eventually** became a successful entrepreneur.
 
 
 
• **Certainly** (निश्चित रूप से): Without any doubt; definitely.
 
 
• **Example:** She **certainly** has the skills needed for this job.
